c.tagline: Botswana's dusty tourism capital and the gateway to the Okavango Delta.

taxi.fareNote: There is no ride-hailing app in Maun. Blue combi minibuses run fixed routes for a flat few pula, while private 'special' taxis are unmetered - agree the fare before setting off. Most visitors rely on lodge transfers and rental 4x4s.

emergency.note: 999 reaches police, 997 the ambulance and 998 fire. Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital is the main hospital, and safari lodges arrange air-ambulance evacuation from remote Delta camps.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty theft from vehicles and campsites occurs; avoid walking alone along unlit roads after dark.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of Maun around the Old Mall and the airport, packed with banks, supermarkets, safari operators and the small Nhabe Museum; the practical, walkable base most visitors use to stock up and arrange trips into the Delta.

A riverside ward southeast of town along the Thamalakane and toward the Boro, lined with lodges, campsites and mokoro (dugout canoe) stations; a relaxed, green base close to the water and the Delta poling routes.

The lodge strip northeast of town on the Shorobe road, where thatched riverside lodges and tree camps overlook the Thamalakane; a scenic, quiet base for sundowners and scenic-flight departures over the Delta.
A residential ward north of the centre near Letsholathebe II Memorial Hospital, with guesthouses and the riverside Sedia hotel; calm and local, an easy drive from the shops and airport.
A traditional local ward across the Thamalakane from the centre, with homes, small eateries and everyday Maun life; the least touristy base, good for travelers wanting an authentic, low-key stay.

water.note: Town supply is treated but variable and sometimes brackish; most visitors stick to bottled or filtered.

transit.pay: Combi fares are a flat few pula paid in cash to the driver; 'special' taxi fares are negotiated before the ride. There is no fare card, pass or app system.
transit.hours: Combis run roughly 6am-7pm and thin out after dark; arrange a taxi or lodge transfer at night.
transit.note: Maun has no rail, metro or formal city bus; locals get around on blue combi minibuses running fixed routes and on shared 'special' taxis, while most visitors rely on lodge transfers, rental 4x4s and taxis. The town is spread out along the river, so walking only really covers the central mall area.

bus: Intercity coaches to Francistown, Gaborone and Kasane/Chobe

transit.m: Taxi or lodge transfer to central Maun (~5 min)
Light-aircraft charter transfer into the Okavango Delta camps

tip.r: Tipping is customary in the safari/lodge sector - roughly $10-20/day for safari guides and mokoro polers; ~10% at restaurants is appreciated.
